chapter: Chicago and New York with Louis Armstrong, 1925-30
title: Connie's Inn under Allie Ross and the WOR commercial program
summary: Zutty went into Connie's Inn with Allie Ross's band and had one of the first commercial radio programs by a Black band, on WOR for a clothing store. Marge and Zutty argue whether it was Dickerson's men.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: And then the next job, when you really started working was in Connie's Inn. That's when we sent for mother and I to come.
Well whose band were you in at Connies Inn?
(All Ross's).
Oh.
We had one of the first commercial programs for Levy over WOR. And we'd have singers like Ada Ward, Clarence Townsend, Ernie Smith and like that.
But it was the Carroll Dickerson band.
It was not the Carroll Dickerson band, it was Ally Ross band.
I say a lot of the boys from the Carroll Dickerson band though.
No, there was nobody in there.
Well there was when Louis was there. But when Louis cut out and left all the boys from Carroll Dickerson's band without a job or anything, that's when Zutty said he was going in....................
In Connie's Inn with Ally Ross.
Yes. But you were in Connie's Inn Zutty.
I had been in Connie's Inn and they wanted me to stay.
But didn't Louis play in Connie's Inn too?
Why sure he did. That's where we played at Connie's Inn?).
Well that's what I say and when Louis cut out they were going to let the band go without any work.
You said that, we were speaking about WOR.
No I'm saying before we got to that when we went to see Louis he had just cut out from Connie's (Carney's Inn) and they let the whole band go. That's when (All Roth?) took over.
That's right.
That's what I'm saying.
That was at Connie's (Carney's Inn)?
That's right.
Really that was the 'Hot Chocolates' Show was it?
That's right, yes.
And that was where Louis really, I mean that's really when Louis took off I think with 'Aint Misbehaving' and those things.
Yes.

I was speaking about the Mo clothing store. And that's why I say we were one of the first black bands to have a commercial. In New York City. And that was (All Roth's?) band but he didn't have none of Dickerson's boys in that.
No, because Louis chucked them.
